summary: Intermittent SSO login loop for Secret Manager console after device-trust probe
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers intermittently cannot access the internal Secret Manager console. After clicking 'Sign in with SSO' they are redirected to the Okta device-trust step; after approving device challenge the browser returns to the Secret Manager page but immediately redirects back to Okta and repeats the device approval prompt (login loop).

Impact: Affects a subset of users who have device-trust enforcement enabled (device-registered via MDM). Blocks access to secret rotation and emergency credential retrieval. Reported by 6 engineers across two teams; on-call and runbook access impacted.

Environment: Production, us-west region, internal console behind identity-proxy and okta-device-trust flow. Not observed in staging.

Steps to reproduce: listed below. Intermittent; not reliably reproducible for all affected users.

Expected behavior: After Okta device approval, users should be returned to Secret Manager with a valid session and RBAC claims.

Observed behavior: Post device approval, redirect loop back to Okta device challenge. When loop breaks, session often lands in a minimal unauthenticated page or immediate 403 from console API requiring re-login.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Click 'Sign in with SSO' -> Okta page loads
3) Okta prompts for device-trust challenge (push or biometrics),
4) Approve device challenge on MDM client,
5) Browser returns to secret manager but immediately redirects back to Okta device-trust prompt (loop)
logs: auth-proxy: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z INFO Received callback from Okta for user priya@redwood.com, state=xyz123
auth-proxy: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z DEBUG Introspecting session cookie: missing 'device_binding' claim
okta-svc: 2026-03-10T14:22:04Z INFO Device challenge accepted for device id dv-9182 for user priya@redwood.com
console-api: 2026-03-10T14:22:04Z WARN Session create returned 403 RBAC: claim 'device_trust' not present
browser-console: Failed to exchange authorization code: 400 - "invalid_grant: code already redeemed" (observed in one trace)
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Priya Menon: Filed after 3 engineers on #infra reported repeated device prompts and inability to retrieve secrets for emergency rotation.

2026-03-10 15:25 - Maya Chen (oncall-auth): Started triage. Reproduced flow once; saw auth-proxy log showing missing 'device_binding' claim even after Okta accepted challenge. Opening deeper traces with identity team.

2026-03-10 17:11 - Rafael Torres (identity): Hypothesis: race between Okta callback processing and session claim enrichment job; device claim sometimes omitted if callback processed by ingress instance without background claim fetch. Added debug logging to claim enrichment path.

2026-03-11 09:40 - Maya Chen: Rolled a temporary mitigation: sticky routing for identity-proxy callbacks to ensure same instance handles callback + claim enrichment. Asking SRE to monitor for recurrence and error rate.

2026-03-12 08:55 - Rafael Torres: Found edge case where multiple concurrent auth callbacks with identical state tokens cause one callback to return early after code redeem (invalid_grant), leaving session incomplete. Preparing PR to serialize callback handling per state token.
investigation_notes: Trace 1 (priay@redwood.com) shows Okta device challenge accepted at 14:22:04 but auth-proxy logged missing device claim at 14:22:03 due to ordering mismatch between callback and background claim fetch.
We observed 'invalid_grant: code already redeemed' in one trace meaning the authorization code was processed twice; second attempt returns 400 and leaves session half-initialized.
Sticky routing reduced recurrence in limited canary (2/6 users stopped looping), indicating a race between instances is likely contributor.
RBAC check on console-api strictly requires 'device_trust' claim; when claim is absent created session rejects with 403 leading client to re-initiate SSO, causing the loop.
No evidence of Okta misconfiguration; device challenge events are recorded as accepted consistently in Okta logs.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: enabled sticky callback routing for identity-proxy and added extra logging around authorization-code handling. Long-term fix: PR to serialize callback handling per OAuth state token (identity-proxy PR 5182) and additional idempotency checks when redeeming auth codes. Requesting rollout to prod us-west during next maintenance window after code review. Follow-up action to add a targeted Canary in us-west for 24h monitoring.
